q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Forecast

## (a) Time left until resolution
The Q2 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for **August 26, 2026** (per the research). Today is August 18, 2026. **8 days remain** until the earnings announcement and guidance release.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 forward guidance will be in the **$90–$95 billion range**, with the company likely issuing guidance very close to its Q1 forward guidance of **$91.0 billion ±2%** (i.e., $89.18–$92.82 billion).

**Reasoning:**
- NVIDIA provided explicit forward guidance of $91.0B ±2% for Q2 FY2027 in its Q1 earnings release on May 20, 2026
- This guidance is only ~3 months old and would typically remain stable unless material business conditions changed
- Analyst consensus ranges from $91.8B to $93.5B, which is only modestly above the company's own guidance—suggesting no major upside surprise is expected
- Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6B (85% YoY growth), and the company's Data Center unit drove 92% of revenue at $75.2B
- NVIDIA's guidance is explicitly conservative, excluding China Data Center compute revenue due to export restrictions
- The company has historically been cautious with guidance to exceed expectations

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Weaker-than-expected demand** in the interim months (though unlikely given the strong Q1 results and continued AI demand)
- **Macro deterioration** or customer capex pullback (not evident in current data)
- **Supply chain disruptions** affecting production capacity (no evidence in provided research)
- **Competitive pressures** intensifying (e.g., AMD, custom chips ramping faster)
- **Geopolitical escalation** extending export restrictions beyond current China policy
- Conservative guidance revision downward if the company sees warning signs post-May

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-anticipated demand** from hyperscalers (e.g., orders exceeding expectations post-Q1)
- **China revenue upside** if geopolitical conditions unexpectedly improve or workarounds emerge
- **Higher ASP** on H100/H200 products or faster transition to next-gen chips driving better margins and revenue
- **Market share gains** from competitors losing ground
- **Inventory correction** leading to accelerated orders (though this seems unlikely given supply constraints)
- **Analyst consensus** ($91.8–$93.5B) suggests the market expects modest upside from the official $91.0B guidance, so the company may raise guidance to beat expectations

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Official Q2 FY2027 forward guidance (May 2026):** $91.0 billion ±2% = **$89.18–$92.82 billion**
- **Analyst consensus:** $91.8–$93.5 billion (slightly above official guidance)
- **Q1 FY2027 actual:** $81.6 billion
- **Q1 guidance was $81.0B ±2%** (implied from the pattern), suggesting NVIDIA typically guides conservatively and beats by ~0.6–2%

## Analysis of the range provided (99.5–115.5 Billion)

The range given (99.5–115.5B) is substantially **higher** than both NVIDIA's own guidance ($91.0B) and analyst consensus ($91.8–93.5B). This appears to be a very wide range designed to capture tail scenarios. The actual forward guidance will almost certainly fall in the **lower half** of this range, likely between 91–95B.

---

**My estimate centers on the official guidance of $91.0B ±2%, with modest upside to ~$92–93B if the company wants to beat expectations marginally:**

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, as of its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026, is **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is slightly higher, with some aggregators pegging it closer to $91.8 billion or even $93.5 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors), [news.ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The company's Data Center unit accounted for 92% of total sales in Q1, reaching $75.2 billion [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/). The Q2 FY2027 results are scheduled for release on August 26, 2026 [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors).
